newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee trade slows amid volatility.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee trade slows amid volatility.

text.p: Vietnam's export coffee prices have risen in tandem with sharp increases on world markets over the past week, but trade has been thin with dealers reluctant to buy or sell amid the volatility, traders said on Friday.
Five percent robusta was quoted on Friday at around $1200-$1250 per tonne FOB Saigon Port against a level of about $1,000 per tonne a week earlier.
"The export market has been totally crazy," said a Ho Chi Minh City trader. "Everybody is in a panic, because nobody can predict the peak of the upturn."

World coffee prices have risen sharply over the past week. On Thursday, London prices rose more than five percent in value before easing slightly on news that producer nations meeting in Brazil had agreed to cut exports by at least one million bags.
Regional dealers said overnight news of an end to the Colombian port workers strike might dampen sentiment on the London market, but any correction in the upswing would likely take several days.
Exporters in Ho Chi Minh City said they had heavy losses over the past week and called the current market "dangerous".
"It's a challenge for us," said one. "But the current market is good only for speculators."
